data.objective: To optimize ground-layer adaptive optics (GLAO) guide star configurations for achieving uniform wide-field resolution in solar observation, and to establish a quantitative evaluation metric (Correlation Evaluation Function, CEF) for assessing the spatial uniformity of corrected image quality across the field of view.
data.novelty: Proposes the Correlation Evaluation Function (CEF) as a new metric specifically designed to quantify wide-field resolution uniformity in GLAO systems. Systematically demonstrates that single-ring guide star configurations can achieve superior uniformity compared to traditional center-plus-ring layouts, challenging conventional wisdom in GLAO design.
data.method: Numerical simulation of atmospheric turbulence using multi-layer phase screens, laboratory-based GLAO experimental validation, and on-sky verification using the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST). Parametric study of guide star configurations including number of stars, ring diameter, and conjugate height.
data.performance metrics: Single-ring GLAO configurations demonstrated superior CEF values (≥0.95 uniformity) across 3-5 guide star arrangements. On-sky verification at NVST confirmed simulated optimal configurations yield consistent wide-field correction with FWHM improvement of 15-25% over uncorrected conditions.

data.objective: To break through the bottleneck of mode number limitation and speckle noise in traditional holographic modal wavefront sensors (HMWS) by developing a deep learning-enhanced architecture capable of high-order aberration detection with improved signal-to-noise ratio.
data.novelty: Introduces a dual-network deep learning architecture that combines modal regression for rapid Zernike coefficient prediction with pixel-level wavefront reconstruction for detailed phase retrieval. Overcomes the fundamental speckle noise and mode capacity limitations of conventional Shack-Michelson interferometer-based HMWS.
data.method: Dual convolutional neural network architecture: Network 1 performs modal regression for Zernike coefficient extraction, Network 2 provides pixel-level wavefront reconstruction. Training on synthetic wavefront data with controlled aberration distributions. Comparison with conventional SMI-HMWS across varying turbulence strengths.
data.performance metrics: Extended mode number from 15 to 50 Zernike modes; improved signal-to-noise ratio by 8 dB under speckle-limited conditions; achieved 95% reconstruction accuracy for high-order aberrations (Z16-Z50) where conventional HMWS fails.

data.objective: To develop a dual closed-loop precision pointing control system based on differential wavefront sensing (DWS) for space-based gravitational wave detection missions (such as LISA and Taiji), achieving sub-microradian pointing stability at milli-Hertz frequencies.
data.novelty: Proposes a novel dual closed-loop DWS architecture that decouples coarse and fine pointing control, combined with an ASD (Amplitude Spectral Density) calibration method for absolute phase-to-angle conversion at ultra-low frequencies (mHz range).
data.method: Differential wavefront sensing with quadrant photodetector, dual-loop control architecture (inner loop fast DWS, outer loop slow fine tracking), ASD calibration for phase-angle transfer function, and experimental validation in simulated space environment.
data.performance metrics: Achieved pointing stability of <100 nrad/√Hz at frequencies above 1 mHz; phase measurement accuracy better than 0.1 mrad; demonstrated compatibility with LISA/Taiji mission requirements for inter-spacecraft laser ranging.

data.objective: To develop a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) capable of fast and accurate wavefront reconstruction under strong turbulence conditions with sparse Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor sub-apertures, enabling real-time deployment on resource-constrained platforms.
data.novelty: Introduces Sub-aperture Information Reuse (SIR) strategy combined with Feature Zeroing Method (FZM) for network compression, achieving dramatic reduction in model size and inference time while maintaining reconstruction accuracy under sparse sampling and strong turbulence.
data.method: Lightweight CNN with sub-aperture parameter sharing across sparse Shack-Hartmann spots; Feature Zeroing Method for network pruning and compression; TensorRT acceleration with FP16 quantization; training on Kolmogorov turbulence phase screen simulations with varying Cn² profiles.
data.performance metrics: Model size: 1.77 MB (compressed from original); inference time: 0.191 ms per frame; reconstruction accuracy within 5% of ResNet-50 baseline; supports >5 kHz closed-loop control rate.

data.objective: To achieve high-fidelity complex field reconstruction (both amplitude and phase) through scattering media using single-pixel blind modulated diffraction imaging, without requiring prior knowledge of the scattering medium's transmission matrix.
data.novelty: Demonstrates single-pixel blind modulated diffraction imaging that combines optical memory effect with computational phase retrieval, enabling high-fidelity complex field recovery through scattering media without calibration or knowledge of scattering properties.
data.method: Single-pixel detector with structured illumination patterns; blind modulation approach leveraging optical memory effect; iterative phase retrieval algorithm combining diffraction propagation constraints; coherent detection scheme for complex field measurement.
data.performance metrics: Achieved complex field reconstruction fidelity >0.9 (normalized correlation); phase retrieval accuracy within λ/10; demonstrated through scattering media with transmission values ranging from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁶.

data.objective: To develop an automated shear parameter determination method for lateral shearing interferometry using transfer learning from a pre-trained TransUNet model, eliminating the need for manual calibration or reference measurements.
data.novelty: First application of TransUNet architecture with transfer learning to lateral shearing interferometry for automatic shear parameter extraction, achieving high precision without requiring reference wavefronts or manual intervention.
data.method: Transfer learning from pre-trained TransUNet encoder-decoder; feature extraction from shearing interferograms; regression network for shear amount and direction estimation; fine-tuning on lateral shearing interferometry datasets with varying shear parameters.
data.performance metrics: Shear parameter estimation accuracy within 1% relative error; demonstrated on synthetic and experimental interferograms; processing time <1 second per interferogram; robust to noise levels up to 10 dB SNR.

data.objective: To develop a closed-loop co-phasing method for segmented mirror telescopes based on dispersed interferogram slope analysis, enabling precise piston error detection and correction across mirror segments.
data.novelty: Proposes using the slope of dispersed interferograms as a robust piston error metric, combined with closed-loop feedback control for real-time segment co-phasing. Overcomes limitations of conventional edge sensors in large segmented telescopes.
data.method: Dispersed broadband interferometry for piston detection; slope analysis of wavelength-dependent interferogram patterns; closed-loop servo control for segment alignment; experimental demonstration on segmented mirror testbed.
data.performance metrics: Piston detection precision within λ/50 (RMS); closed-loop co-phasing accuracy better than 20 nm; demonstrated on 7-segment mirror array; robust against atmospheric seeing and mechanical vibrations.

data.objective: To investigate multi-wavelength Zernike wavefront sensors for improving dynamic range and photon noise robustness in extreme adaptive optics systems designed for direct exoplanet imaging.
data.novelty: Systematic analysis of multi-wavelength Zernike wavefront sensor operation, demonstrating that simultaneous measurements at multiple wavelengths significantly extend dynamic range while improving photon noise resilience compared to single-wavelength implementations.
data.method: Multi-wavelength Zernike wavefront sensor simulation; photon noise propagation analysis; comparison with single-wavelength configurations; optimization of wavelength spacing and number of channels; performance evaluation under realistic photon flux conditions.
data.performance metrics: Extended dynamic range by factor of 3-5 compared to single-wavelength sensor; improved photon noise limited sensitivity by 2-3 dB; demonstrated for wavefront error regimes from λ/100 to λ/2.

data.objective: To develop a single-shot quantum wavefront sensing method using position-correlated photon pairs and a Shack-Hartmann sensor, enabling quantum-enhanced adaptive imaging without requiring scanning or multiple exposures.
data.novelty: First demonstration of single-shot quantum wavefront sensing combining spatially entangled photon pairs with Shack-Hartmann detection, enabling simultaneous measurement of pump and idler wavefronts for quantum adaptive imaging.
data.method: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion for photon pair generation; position-correlated detection using split Shack-Hartmann sensor; single-shot wavefront reconstruction from coincidence measurements; quantum image correction using correlated wavefront information.
data.performance metrics: Single-shot wavefront measurement accuracy within λ/20; demonstrated quantum enhancement factor of 1.5-2× in signal-to-noise ratio; achieved at photon flux levels compatible with practical imaging scenarios.

data.objective: To develop a low-frequency heterodyne interferometry method for accurate calibration of liquid crystal spatial light modulator (LC-SLM) phase response characteristics, addressing nonlinearities and hysteresis effects.
data.novelty: Proposes low-frequency heterodyne interferometry as a calibration technique for LC-SLM phase response, providing high-accuracy phase characterization at operational speeds compatible with real-time adaptive optics applications.
data.method: Low-frequency heterodyne interferometry with acousto-optic modulators; phase-locked detection of LC-SLM modulation response; characterization of phase-voltage relationship and temporal dynamics; comparison with conventional calibration methods.
data.performance metrics: Phase calibration accuracy within 0.5% of 2π range; demonstrated linearity improvement from ±5% to ±1% after calibration; temporal response characterization accuracy better than 10 μs; applicable across full LC-SLM operating wavelength range.

data.objective: To develop an integrated Mach-Zehnder wavefront sensor for extreme adaptive optics on giant telescopes, enabling simultaneous wavefront sensing and starlight suppression for direct exoplanet imaging.
data.novelty: First integrated photonic Mach-Zehnder wavefront sensor combining wavefront sensing with starlight nulling in a single compact device, enabling simultaneous correction and high-contrast imaging on giant telescope platforms.
data.method: Photonic integrated circuit implementation of Mach-Zehnder interferometer; broadband nulling for starlight suppression; integrated phase detection for wavefront sensing; coupling to adaptive optics correction loop; performance characterization on optical testbed.
data.performance metrics: Null depth >10⁻³ across 10% bandwidth; wavefront sensing accuracy within λ/100; device footprint <10×10 mm; compatible with 30-40m giant telescope secondary mirror correction requirements.

data.objective: To improve Shack-Hartmann wavefront reconstruction algorithms for handling shock-distorted wavefronts caused by strong atmospheric turbulence, where conventional centroid methods fail due to spot merging and splitting.
data.novelty: Develops robust wavefront reconstruction algorithms specifically designed for shock-distorted wavefronts, introducing spot pattern recognition and adaptive centroid correction methods that maintain accuracy under strong turbulence conditions.
data.method: Modified centroid detection with spot pattern classification; adaptive window sizing based on local turbulence strength; iterative wavefront reconstruction with shock correction; comparison with conventional center-of-mass and weighted centroid algorithms.
data.performance metrics: Maintained wavefront reconstruction accuracy within 15% of weak turbulence performance at Fried parameter r₀ < 5 cm; spot detection success rate >90% under shock conditions; 3× improvement in strong turbulence regime compared to standard algorithms.

data.objective: To develop a model-based tilt correction method for segmented space telescopes using extended beacon sources, enabling fine pointing stabilization for high-contrast imaging without requiring point-like guide stars.
data.novelty: Proposes extended beacon-based tilt sensing combined with model-based control for segmented space telescopes, overcoming the limitation of requiring unresolved point sources for fine guidance in coronagraphic imaging applications.
data.method: Extended beacon wavefront sensing using focal plane images; model-based tilt estimation algorithm accounting for segment geometry and segment-level aberrations; predictive control for tilt correction; simulation validation with JWST-like configurations.
data.performance metrics: Tilt correction residual <1 mas (milliarcsecond) RMS; demonstrated with extended beacons up to 0.5 arcsecond angular size; compatible with coronagraphic imaging requirements for exoplanet detection at contrast levels <10⁻⁸.

data.objective: To compare and evaluate different wavefront sensing algorithms for solar Hα prominence observation, specifically assessing correlation-based methods versus tie-point methods for measuring atmospheric seeing conditions.
data.novelty: Systematic comparison of wavefront sensing algorithms specifically tailored for solar Hα prominence imaging, demonstrating that cross-correlation methods achieve superior signal-to-noise ratio compared to traditional tie-point approaches.
data.method: Cross-correlation algorithm for image shift measurement; tie-point feature tracking method; signal-to-noise analysis under varying solar prominence contrast conditions; experimental comparison using solar telescope Hα imaging system.
data.performance metrics: Cross-correlation method achieved 3× higher signal-to-noise ratio than tie-point method; wavefront measurement accuracy within λ/8 for solar Hα observations; demonstrated improvement in solar adaptive optics correction quality.

data.objective: To develop a symmetric genetic algorithm for fast wavefront correction of entangled photon pairs, enabling efficient optimization of spatial light modulator patterns for quantum communication and quantum imaging applications.
data.novelty: Introduces symmetric genetic algorithm specifically designed for entangled photon wavefront correction, exploiting the symmetric correlation structure of photon pairs to accelerate optimization convergence by 5-10× compared to standard genetic algorithms.
data.method: Symmetric genetic algorithm with paired optimization of signal and idler wavefronts; spatial light modulator for phase modulation; Hong-Ou-Mandel interference as optimization metric; parallel evaluation of entangled photon correlations.
data.performance metrics: Optimization convergence time reduced from 30 minutes to 3-5 minutes; achieved entanglement preservation fidelity >0.95 after correction; demonstrated quantum state fidelity improvement of 40% in turbulent channel.

data.objective: To provide a comprehensive review of rotational adaptive optics (RAO) techniques that exploit field rotation in astronomical telescopes to achieve wider-field atmospheric turbulence correction.
data.novelty: First comprehensive review synthesizing the state-of-the-art in rotational adaptive optics, establishing a unified framework for understanding field-rotation-based turbulence correction across different telescope configurations.
data.method: Literature review and synthesis; theoretical analysis of field rotation mechanics in alt-azimuth telescopes; comparison of RAO approaches including ground-layer and multi-conjugate configurations; assessment of technical requirements and limitations.
data.performance metrics: Reviewed correction Strehl ratios from 0.1-0.8 depending on field angle and turbulence conditions; identified RAO as providing 2-3× wider corrected field compared to conventional AO; assessed current technical readiness levels from TRL 3-6.

data.objective: To develop a sparse blind deconvolution computational adaptive optics method for improving fluorescence microscopy image quality without requiring hardware wavefront sensing or modification.
data.novelty: Proposes sparse blind deconvolution as a computational adaptive optics technique that simultaneously estimates both the aberrated point spread function and the object structure, enabling post-acquisition aberration correction in fluorescence microscopy.
data.method: Sparse regularization-based blind deconvolution algorithm; joint estimation of PSF and object using alternating minimization; sparse prior constraints on both PSF and object distributions; validation on simulated and experimental fluorescence microscopy data.
data.performance metrics: Achieved 2-3× improvement in image resolution (FWHM reduction); demonstrated Strehl ratio recovery from 0.2 to >0.7; processing time <5 minutes for 3D datasets; validated on biological samples with various aberration strengths.

data.objective: To re-examine and improve differential optical transfer function (dOTF) wavefront sensing for high-contrast imaging applications, addressing systematic errors and sensitivity limitations in practical implementations.
data.novelty: Provides critical re-evaluation of dOTF technique identifying previously unrecognized systematic error sources; proposes improved calibration and measurement protocols that restore dOTF sensitivity to theoretical limits for high-contrast imaging.
data.method: Detailed error analysis of dOTF measurement chain; improved calibration using phase diversity; systematic investigation of detector non-linearity, chromatic effects, and temporal instability; comparison with other focal plane sensing techniques.
data.performance metrics: Improved dOTF accuracy from λ/20 to λ/100 through calibration; demonstrated non-common path aberration measurement sensitivity <1 nm; validated for coronagraphic imaging at contrast levels <10⁻⁸.

data.objective: To develop a weighted modal control method that utilizes partial slope information from Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors to improve wavefront correction efficiency and reduce computational requirements.
data.novelty: Proposes weighted modal control approach that selectively uses partial slope measurements based on signal quality weights, enabling more efficient wavefront correction with reduced computational load while maintaining or improving correction performance.
data.method: Weighted modal reconstruction using partial slope measurements; signal-to-noise based weighting of sub-aperture contributions; modal control matrix optimization; experimental validation on adaptive optics testbed.
data.performance metrics: Reduced computational requirements by 40% while maintaining correction quality; improved Strehl ratio by 10-15% in low signal-to-noise conditions; demonstrated real-time operation at >1 kHz update rate.

data.objective: To utilize AI-based phase modulation techniques to mitigate pointing errors in free space optical communication links, improving beam tracking and maintaining communication quality under atmospheric turbulence conditions.
data.novelty: Introduces AI-driven adaptive phase modulation for real-time pointing error compensation in free space optical communication, combining deep learning prediction with adaptive optics correction for proactive rather than reactive error mitigation.
data.method: Deep learning-based pointing error prediction from wavefront measurements; adaptive phase modulation using spatial light modulator; predictive control algorithm for beam tracking; experimental validation on free space optical link testbed.
data.performance metrics: Reduced pointing error variance by 60-70%; maintained communication link availability >99.5% under strong turbulence conditions; demonstrated bit error rate improvement from 10⁻³ to 10⁻⁶; response time <1 ms for atmospheric-induced pointing fluctuations.

data.objective: To develop a noise-robust multi-fringe decomposition algorithm for lateral shearing interferometry that accurately separates and analyzes complex fringe patterns under low signal-to-noise conditions.
data.novelty: Introduces robust multi-fringe decomposition algorithm specifically designed for noisy lateral shearing interferograms, achieving accurate fringe separation and phase extraction where conventional methods fail due to noise and fringe complexity.
data.method: Multi-component fringe decomposition using frequency-domain analysis; adaptive noise filtering based on local fringe frequency; iterative phase extraction with noise robustness constraints; validation on simulated and experimental interferograms.
data.performance metrics: Maintained phase extraction accuracy within λ/15 at SNR as low as 5 dB; demonstrated 3× improvement in noise tolerance compared to conventional FFT-based methods; processing time <0.5 seconds per interferogram.

data.objective: To investigate and demonstrate the effectiveness of real-time adaptive optics compensation combined with phase gradient autofocus (PGA) for mitigating atmospheric turbulence effects on inverse synthetic aperture ladar (ISAL) imaging.
data.novelty: First systematic study combining adaptive optics with PGA for ISAL turbulence mitigation, demonstrating that AO at the optical front-end significantly improves subsequent digital autofocus performance in strong turbulence conditions.
data.method: Dynamic phase screen simulation of atmospheric turbulence; Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor based AO correction; phase gradient autofocus algorithm for residual phase correction; range-Doppler imaging algorithm; combined AO-PGA processing pipeline.
data.performance metrics: AO bandwidth requirement identified: >60 Hz effective for strong turbulence (r₀=0.03m, v=5m/s); combined AO-PGA achieved ISAL image quality improvement of 10-15 dB in peak signal-to-side-lobe ratio; demonstrated imaging capability at turbulence strengths where uncompensated systems fail.

data.objective: To develop field-conjugate adaptive optics (FCAO) for GRIN-lens microendoscopy, extending the corrected field of view for deep brain two-photon imaging beyond the limitations of conventional pupil-conjugate adaptive optics.
data.novelty: First demonstration of field-conjugate adaptive optics specifically designed for GRIN-lens microendoscopy, achieving extended field-of-view correction by placing the wavefront modulator at a field-conjugate plane rather than the pupil plane.
data.method: Field-conjugate adaptive optics with wavefront modulator at field-conjugate plane; wavefront-sensorless image-based optimization using Gaussian ring basis functions; two-photon microscopy with galvo-galvo scanning; in vivo validation in awake mice.
data.performance metrics: Extended corrected field of view from 140 μm to 350 μm diameter; 2.5-3× intensity improvement at edge fields; maintained Strehl ratio >0.8 across extended FOV; demonstrated in vivo deep brain imaging with improved edge field quality.

data.objective: To develop a data-driven optimization framework combined with digital twin technology for the design and real-time performance monitoring of large aperture mirror systems, reducing computational cost while maintaining design quality.
data.novelty: Integrates constrained multi-objective optimization (CNSGAIII-EHVI) with digital twin platform for large aperture mirror systems, achieving efficient design space exploration with minimal finite element analysis calls while providing real-time performance visualization.
data.method: 45-dimensional parameterized mirror model; CNSGAIII-EHVI constrained multi-objective optimization; RBF surrogate model for rapid response; Unity3D-based digital twin visualization; node reduction technique for computational efficiency.
data.performance metrics: Reduced FEA calls from thousands to 100; surrogate model R² >0.999; digital twin response time <2 seconds (vs. 240 seconds for full FEA); achieved 32 feasible Pareto-optimal designs from 100 evaluations.

data.objective: To develop a deep learning-based single-shot lateral shearing interferometry method that can simultaneously extract wavefront information in two orthogonal shear directions from a single composite interferogram.
data.novelty: First demonstration of deep learning-based single-shot lateral shearing interferometry that separates composite x-y shear information from a single captured interferogram, eliminating the need for sequential measurements or rotating components.
data.method: Polarization grating-based dual-direction shearing interferometer; pixelated polarizer camera for phase-shifted interferogram capture; modified DYnet++ neural network for fringe pattern separation; training on deformable mirror-generated wavefront datasets.
data.performance metrics: Phase measurement accuracy within λ/14 RMS for complex surfaces; single-shot acquisition enables dynamic measurements up to video frame rate; demonstrated noise robustness up to 40% Gaussian noise after retraining; model parameters: 20 million (halved from original DYnet++).
